note: Rigor slot. 'Yes' is now the rational-means-terminating misconception; 'truncated' is a separate error path.
q:
Maya uses a calculator to find 190/33. The calculator shows 5.757575758. Maya says that 190/33 = 5.757575758.

Is Maya correct? Choose the statement that is true.
opts: Yes. 190/33 is a rational number, so its decimal must end, and 5.757575758 is where it ends.
No. 190/33 = 5.75, a repeating decimal. The calculator rounded the last digit it could show.
No. The calculator cut off the digits it could not show, so the exact value is 5.757575757, with no more digits after that.
No. The decimal never ends, so 190/33 is not a rational number and has no exact value.
s: 190 ÷ 33 = 5.757575…; the block 75 repeats forever, so the exact value is 5.75. The display holds 9 decimal places. The tenth digit is 5, so the ninth digit 7 rounds up to 8. The display is rounded, not exact. A fraction of two integers is rational even when its decimal repeats, so Maya is not correct.
why: believes every rational number has a terminating decimal; 190/33 repeats forever
treats the display as cut off and a 9-place decimal as exact; the next digit is 5, so the 7 rounded up to 8, and no terminating decimal equals 190/33
believes a repeating decimal is irrational; a ratio of two integers is rational and 190/33 is its exact value

q:
A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. Mia has a scoop that holds 0.3 cup when it is full, and she can use part of a scoop. She needs to know how many scoops to use.

Which statement is correct?
opts: Rewrite 2/3 as 0.66. Then 0.66 ÷ 0.3 = 2.2, so she needs exactly 2.2 scoops.
Rewrite 0.3 as 3/10. Then 2/3 ÷ 3/10 = 2 2/9, so she needs a little more than 2 scoops.
Rewrite 0.3 as 1/3. Then 2/3 ÷ 1/3 = 2, so she needs exactly 2 scoops.
Rewrite 0.3 as 3/10. Then 3/10 ÷ 2/3 = 9/20, so she needs less than 1 scoop.
